title: Move Zeroes
statement: Move every 0 in `nums` to the end while preserving the relative order of the nonzero elements. Return the rearranged array.
hints: A stable filter of nonzeros, followed by zeros, is correct and uses extra memory.
A write pointer marks the next position that should hold a nonzero.
After copying nonzeros forward, fill the tail with zeros. Swapping works too and keeps the algorithm in place.

approaches.name: In-place write pointer
approaches.explanation: Compact nonzeros, then zero-fill the suffix.

editorial: The write pointer is the classic stable partition. Every nonzero is copied to the next write slot and the pointer advances. The number of leftover slots is the number of zeros, so a second short loop fills them. Order of nonzeros is unchanged because they are copied left to right.
